elements.element: Governing law is the laws of the State of New York
elements.evidence: "governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County
elements.evidence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction"

elements.element: Law and forum form a single permitted corresponding pair (no residual Singapore forum)
elements.evidence: Singapore law and "the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction" deleted from 28.1

elements.element: Alternative permitted law: Delaware, California, or England and Wales
elements.evidence: "laws of the State of New York" — not a fallback jurisdiction

elements.element: Alternative permitted forum: Delaware/California courts or courts of London
elements.evidence: "courts located in New York County, New York" — not a fallback forum

offending_extra_words: Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York to protect
reasons: Preferred level is fully achieved: 28.1 now selects New York law and 28.2 retains exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County, forming one permitted corresponding pair.
The conflicting Singapore law and forum wording was removed by a targeted replacement of 28.1, which is the minimum edit needed.

The second operation is not needed to complete the preferred position. Confining the interim-injunctive carve-out to New York County courts narrows a pre-existing mutual protection (the ability to seek temporary relief in any court with jurisdiction, e.g. where infringement or a data breach occurs) and goes beyond fixing the law/forum pair.
No undefined terms, contradictions, or dangling mechanics are introduced, and all other sentences of 28.2 remain effective; the intent of the surrounding clause is preserved.
Recommendation: drop operation 2 and leave the original injunctive-relief carve-out untouched.
